decisions.quote: This research was designed with two key goals in mind. First, we wanted to examine whether the good psychometric properties of the original BFI–2 would replicate in samples of Dutch adults.
decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and blind coding agree that the study is a replication collecting new data from Dutch samples to re-test the published psychometric findings for the English BFI-2.

decisions.quote: Soto and John (2017b) investigated the psychometric properties of the English-language BFI–2, using U.S. samples. They found evidence for the reliability, structure, and convergent and predictive validity of the instrument.
decisions.location: Introduction, The Big Five Inventory–2: Development and psychometric properties, p. 313
decisions.reason: The primary replication target is Soto and John (2017b), 'The next big five inventory (BFI-2): Developing and assessing a hierarchical model with 15 facets to enhance bandwidth, fidelity, and predictive power' (DOI: 10.1037/pspp0000096), which matches both the shipped original and blind target 0.

decisions.quote: Overall, we replicated the support that Soto and John (2017b) reported for the structural validity of the English BFI–2, as well as the convergent validity and internal consistency of its domain and facet scales.
decisions.reason: Both the shipped quote from the Abstract ('Results indicated that the structure found in the English version was replicated in the Dutch adaptation.') and the overall conclusion statement in the Discussion confirm that the replication outcome for Soto and John (2017b) is successful.

decisions.quote: Besides the 60-item version, Soto and John (2017a) published short (30-item) and extra-short (15-item) versions of the BFI–2, with acceptable to good reliabilities for short Big Five domain scales. Table 2 also displays the Cronbach’s alphas of these shorter scales in the Dutch adaptation.
decisions.reason: Not an omitted target (materials/measure citation only). The authors administered the 60-item BFI-2 to replicate Soto and John (2017b) and only cited the sibling paper Soto and John (2017a) in a single paragraph of Study 1's reliability analysis to define the 30-item and 15-item subsets scored for descriptive Cronbach's alphas in Table 2, without testing their structure or validity or framing Soto and John (2017a) as a replication target in the study aims or conclusion.
